newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Bimantara set on car production.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Bimantara set on car production.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Citra Mobil Nasional said the labor strikes in South Korea had no impact on its sedan production there, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.

The company, a subsidiary of conglomerate Bimantara Citra, produces the 1,500cc and 1,600cc Bimantara Cakra and Bimantara Nenggala sedans in conjunction with Hyundai Motors of South Korea. The cars are manufactured in South Korea.
Bimantara Citra is controlled by Indonesian President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo.
Antara quoted Jongkie Sugiarto, Citra Mobil Nasional president, as saying on Friday the strikes had not affected the company, but might if they continue for more than five months.
South Korean workers in several sectors have struck for nearly a month in protest against a new labour law.
Sugiarto said 2,100 sedans of both types had been sold in the past five months. He said the company expected to sell 2,500 sedans this year. Antara gave no other details.
Citra Mobil Nasional is currently building an assembly plant near Jakarta.

A company controlled by another son of Suharto, Hutomo Mandala Putra, also produces sedans. The company, PT Timor Putra Nasional, produces the Timor sedan, which has won the status of "national car" entitling it to tax breaks that have been contested by Japan, the U.S. and European nations.
The Timor is manufactured in partnership with Kia Motors of South Korea.
